notes:
Summary: Enterprise insurer evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for agent-assist and document search. Primary constraints: EU data residency, customer-managed key requirements, auditable key rotation, and redactable audit logs. CISO requires mTLS + client certs for all server-to-server calls and enforcement of TLS1.3. Prefer AWS KMS BYOK for cloud, Luna HSM for on-prem. Wants proof that keys never leave HSM and that Redwood can integrate with their key-access proxy.

Security posture needs: strong in-transit encryption with mutual TLS, end-to-end at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys, documented key rotation process (automated rotation + emergency rotation), secrets management integration (Vault), and SIEM-friendly audit logging with redaction filters.

Quoted: "We cannot accept provider-controlled KEKs — keys must be under our custody or HSM-managed with strict access controls." — CISO (Anna Müller).

encryption_posture_summary: In-transit: mutual TLS (mTLS) enforced for all API and internal service RPCs; TLS1.3 minimum. Client cert provisioning via enterprise CA or Redwood-issued certs under customer CSR. At-rest: AES-256 encryptions of model artifacts and KV cache. Customer-managed envelope keys backed by provider KMS (AWS KMS) or BYOK HSM (Luna). Key rotation: support for automated rotation (AWS KMS rotation) plus out-of-band emergency rotation flow and documented re-wrap procedure. Secrets management: recommended HashiCorp Vault integration for short-lived credentials; Redwood will mount secrets via VPC endpoint with IAM role binding. Audit logging: structured JSON logs shipped to customer SIEM (Splunk) via secure syslog forwarder; sensitive fields redacted per regex rules; retention adjustable per policy. Data residency: dedicated control plane in eu-central-1 and data plane nodes pinned to EU subnets.
